source.snippet: For my backups I use restic and sync the restic repository data to S3. Even if the source data is corrupted, I can always roll back to the set of S3 object versions from a particular time. The downside to using S3 object versioning is that I haven't found any good tools to work with object versions across multiple objects.

problem_statement: DevOps engineers and sysadmins using AWS S3 object versioning for ransomware-resistant backups cannot efficiently browse, compare, restore, or manage versioned objects across large multi-object repositories — no purpose-built tooling exists for this workflow.
target_segment: DevOps engineers and sysadmins at SMBs and startups managing S3-based backup strategies with object versioning enabled
notes: Buyer context: teams already paying for AWS S3 storage (recurring cost) and investing engineering time in backup infrastructure — a classic 'we pay for this and it's still painful' signal. The gap is tooling around an existing paid service. Signal is a single 2022 HN comment but the underlying AWS S3 versioning limitation is a durable, well-known gap. Lower signal_strength (2) due to age and single data point; worth pairing with fresher validation before building.
